review_type: Independent AI technical code and regression-test review; reviewer did not author this fix or tests
scope: PlaquePreviewPanel.fetch_papers batch-local destination allocation when all three existing label candidates collide.

findings.detail: The for-else extension runs only after every existing candidate was rejected. Starting above the already-tried numeric index, it increments the suffix until the case-normalized label is absent. Since taken contains finitely many prior labels and numeric suffixes strictly increase, search terminates.

The first three existing candidate labels, lower() policy, destination construction, async reader scheduling, status/translation strings and public documentation are preserved. There is no filesystem probe in the new allocation path.

The three regression scenarios trigger exhaustion of the historical candidates, an additional occupied suffix chain, and case-normalized collisions. Unique destinations plus distinct actual PNG pixels check for output overwrites, not merely internal chosen strings.

Each scenario rereads the same ordered batch and asserts identical destinations, updated expected pixels and unchanged original PDF bytes. This proves deterministic reuse for that batch; it does not claim identity tracking across reordered or unrelated batches.
Independent AST comparison confirms all source outside fetch_papers remains unchanged; all comments and docstrings remain identical. Recorder and source-adapter methods are untouched.

limitations: Only the figure reader is stubbed; tests use real AppScreen, asynchronous job handling, filesystem and PNG readback.
No actual PDF parser, scientific model, native desktop capture, cross-platform hardware or unrelated existing-directory identity behavior is certified.
No duplicate tests, generator, catalog changes or publication performed by reviewer.
